Classified Neighbors Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_classified_neighbors.Rd

Classified neighbors centrality (Li et al. 2018) is a weighted degree in which each neighbor counts according to where it stands in the k-shell decomposition relative to the node: $$k_{CN}(i) = \alpha\,e_u + \beta\,e_{eu} + \gamma\,e_{el} + \mu\,e_l,$$ where \(e_u\) counts the neighbors in a higher shell, \(e_{eu}\) those in the same shell removed in the same step or later, \(e_{el}\) those in the same shell removed earlier, and \(e_l\) those in a lower shell.

Usage

centrality_classified_neighbors(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses cn_weights (the weights of the four classes of neighbors).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The decomposition removes nodes in batches, and the batch number is the layer of the "onion" measure of centrality. A neighbor removed in the same batch counts as "same shell, later": the table of the source's example classifies it so, while its algorithm listing would leave it out. cn_weights holds the four weights in the order of the formula. The default is c(0.4, 0.35, 0.25, 0.1), equation (4) of the source; the source then divides them by their sum, which changes the scores by one constant and no rank. Isolated nodes score 0. The implementation reproduces the class of every neighbor in the source's 14-node example. A cn_weights that is not four finite nonnegative numbers, not all zero, raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Li, C., Wang, L., Sun, S. and Xia, C. (2018). Identification of influential spreaders based on classified neighbors in real-world complex networks. Applied Mathematics and Computation, 320, 512-523. doi:10.1016/j.amc.2017.10.001 .

See also

centrality_coreness, centrality_iksd, centrality.

Examples

centrality_classified_neighbors(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>       1.65       1.80       2.15       1.70       1.65       1.65       1.40 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>       1.65       1.80       1.65
